units.source_text: 且说藤壶妃子此时正乞假归宁，住在外家。

en.t: Now Lady Fujitsubo had taken leave to visit her parents and was staying at her family home.

units.source_text: 源氏公子照例东钻西营，忙于寻求幽会的机缘。

en.t: Prince Genji, as usual, was busy trying every possible way to find a chance for a secret meeting.

units.source_text: 因此左大臣家嫌他久疏，怨声鼎沸。

en.t: Because of this, the household of the Minister of the Left resented his long neglect, and complaints rose loudly there.

units.source_text: 又因觅得了那株细草，外人将二条院新近迎来一个女子的消息传入左大臣家，葵姬便更加生气了。

en.t: Moreover, after he had found that young grass, word reached the Minister of the Left's household that a woman had recently been brought to the Nijo residence, and Lady Aoi became still angrier.

units.source_text: 源氏公子寻思：“紫姬还是个孩子，葵姬不悉此种详情，因而生气，也是难怪的。

en.t: Prince Genji thought, "Lady Murasaki is still a child, and since Lady Aoi does not know the circumstances, it is no wonder that she is angry.

units.source_text: 但她倘能直直爽爽，像普通女子一般向我诉恨，我也一定毫不隐讳，将实情告知，并且安慰她。

en.t: But if she could speak frankly and complain to me like an ordinary woman, I would certainly hide nothing, tell her the truth, and comfort her.

units.source_text: 无奈此人并不亲密，总是往坏里猜测，所猜想的竟是我难以想象之事。

en.t: Unfortunately, she is not intimate with me and always suspects the worst, imagining things that I can hardly even conceive.

units.source_text: 我也只得置之不顾，去干那些不应该干的事了。

en.t: So I have no choice but to leave her aside and go off to do things I ought not to do.

units.source_text: 然而看这个人的样子，并无缺陷，也没有分明可指的瑕疵。

en.t: Yet when I look at her, there is no defect in her, nor any clear flaw one could point to.

units.source_text: 况且是我最初结缡的发妻，所以我真心爱她，又重视她。

en.t: Besides, she is the first wife I married, so I truly love her and value her highly.

units.source_text: 她若不能理解我这点真心，我也无可如何。

en.t: If she cannot understand this sincerity of mine, there is nothing I can do.

units.source_text: 但希望她终于能谅解我而改变态度。”

en.t: Still, I hope that in the end she will understand me and change her attitude."

units.source_text: 葵姬稳重自持，毫无轻率之态，源氏公子对她的信任，自然与众不同。

en.t: Lady Aoi was composed and self-possessed, without the slightest trace of rashness, so Prince Genji's trust in her was naturally unlike his trust in others.
